correctness.rationale: The exact four-state post-loss transition matrix is stochastic; its stationary one- and two-label moment balances imply Pi=t(s-t)/(4-2s+t). Solving the independent three-state killed-chain first-step equations yields H=((5-s)t+4-2s)/(t(s-t)). At fixed sum s, feasible product t is exactly [s-1,s^2/4]. Pi has a strictly decreasing derivative numerator and H a strictly increasing derivative numerator, giving unique projected stationary and hitting optima. Endpoint factorization and monotonic cubic root arguments produce four distinct thresholds and the exact budget discrepancy interval. A standalone Fraction-based linear-system replay corroborates 20031 exact-rational assertions and numerical finite-mesh checks. Its finite tests do not prove the universal derivative statements; the symbolic proof does.

value.rationale: Type-specific loss probabilities are a proposed natural generalization of the 2026 careless-collector model. The minimal nontrivial two-type problem has two operationally different objectives—stationary all-present uptime and time to first coverage—and the finding fully classifies both over a natural fixed loss budget. The two objectives have distinct sharp equality/interior/boundary optimizer thresholds, provably disagree on an explicit open budget interval, and the rational B=1/2 witness demonstrates that a stationarity proxy can select a strictly slower first-completion design. This is a complete, motivated finite-state classification rather than an isolated arbitrary numerical slice.
